purpose: Required review contracts for every production Rust file that crosses an unsafe/Win32/FFI boundary. Classification is not proof of soundness; it prevents unaudited unsafe surface growth.

apps/consent-broker/src/main.rs.safety_invariant: UTF-16 buffers passed to MessageBoxW remain NUL-terminated and alive for the call; language queries use value-returning Win32 APIs only.
apps/consent-broker/src/main.rs.ownership: No returned owning HANDLE or heap pointer crosses this boundary.
apps/consent-broker/src/main.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: PCWSTR pointers are derived from live Vec<u16> storage and are not retained by Win32.
apps/consent-broker/src/main.rs.error_translation: User choice is treated as data; absence/rejection never elevates authority.
apps/consent-broker/src/main.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: No external resource survives a failed dialog/language query.
apps/consent-broker/src/main.rs.cancellation: Consent remains one-shot and cancellation/rejection is fail-closed.

apps/desktop/src/main.rs.safety_invariant: SHELLEXECUTEINFOW and token/process structures are fully initialized, backing UTF-16 buffers outlive ShellExecuteExW, and returned process handles are validated before use.
apps/desktop/src/main.rs.ownership: Any hProcess returned by ShellExecuteExW is immediately transferred to an RAII owner and closed exactly once.
apps/desktop/src/main.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: Pointers reference stack/Vec storage valid through the synchronous API call; structure cbSize values match their concrete type.
apps/desktop/src/main.rs.error_translation: Win32/HRESULT failures propagate as typed application errors rather than being interpreted as success.
apps/desktop/src/main.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: Early returns rely on RAII for process/token handles; no elevation authority is retained after failure.
apps/desktop/src/main.rs.cancellation: Broker launch cannot bypass the surrounding consent/update authorization state machines.

apps/update-broker/src/main.rs.safety_invariant: Dialog string pointers are NUL-terminated, live for MessageBoxW, and only an explicit affirmative result authorizes continuation.
apps/update-broker/src/main.rs.ownership: No owning Win32 resource is returned.
apps/update-broker/src/main.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: PCWSTR pointers remain valid for the duration of the call.
apps/update-broker/src/main.rs.error_translation: Non-affirmative outcomes are rejection, never implicit approval.
apps/update-broker/src/main.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: No resource is retained on rejection or API failure.
apps/update-broker/src/main.rs.cancellation: Cancellation remains fail-closed before installer authority is invoked.

crates/cleaner/src/windows_impl.rs.safety_invariant: Handles are opened with intended access/share/reparse semantics; variable-size file-information/final-path buffers use returned lengths and never read beyond initialized storage.
crates/cleaner/src/windows_impl.rs.ownership: CreateFileW handles transfer immediately to RAII and are closed exactly once.
crates/cleaner/src/windows_impl.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: FILE_ID_INFO/BY_HANDLE_FILE_INFORMATION/output buffers are correctly initialized/aligned and pointer lengths are bounded by Vec capacity.
crates/cleaner/src/windows_impl.rs.error_translation: Win32 failures remain typed errors and identity mismatches are rejection, not fallback deletion.
crates/cleaner/src/windows_impl.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: RAII closes handles on every early return; delete operations revalidate identity immediately before mutation.
crates/cleaner/src/windows_impl.rs.cancellation: No cancellation path may skip final path/identity/reparse defenses.

crates/contracts/build.rs.safety_invariant: Process environment mutation occurs only inside the single-threaded build-script execution context before dependent compiler work is spawned.
crates/contracts/build.rs.ownership: No raw operating-system resource is owned.
crates/contracts/build.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: No raw pointers/buffers cross this boundary.
crates/contracts/build.rs.error_translation: Build setup failure aborts code generation.
crates/contracts/build.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: Environment changes are confined to the build process.
crates/contracts/build.rs.cancellation: Build termination abandons the process-local environment with no runtime authority impact.

crates/crash-diagnostics/src/windows_imp.safety_invariant: EVT_HANDLEs and render buffers are size-probed, resized from authoritative byte counts, aligned for EVT_VARIANT access, and indexed only within returned element counts.
crates/crash-diagnostics/src/windows_imp.ownership: Every EVT_HANDLE is wrapped/closed exactly once; borrowed event handles are not used after collection scope ends.
crates/crash-diagnostics/src/windows_imp.buffer_alignment_lifetime: Pointer arithmetic stays within initialized render storage and typed views respect alignment and reported used length.
crates/crash-diagnostics/src/windows_imp.error_translation: Evt* errors and malformed variants become diagnostic errors/unknown fields, never fabricated health evidence.
crates/crash-diagnostics/src/windows_imp.partial_failure_cleanup: Event/result/context handles close through RAII after partial render failures.
crates/crash-diagnostics/src/windows_imp.cancellation: Bounded query timeouts are preserved; cancellation/timeout cannot leave event handles unclosed.

crates/driver-install/src/lib.rs.safety_invariant: GetTickCount64 is value-returning and converted with saturating timestamp arithmetic.
crates/driver-install/src/lib.rs.error_translation: Arithmetic is saturating and cannot wrap into fabricated boot state.
crates/driver-install/src/lib.rs.cancellation: No blocking/cancellable operation crosses this boundary.

crates/hardware-telemetry/src/windows_im.safety_invariant: Win32/WMI structs carry required size fields, COM variants are interpreted by type, DeviceIoControl output sizes bound parser reads, and ATA/NVMe byte parsing never exceeds returned buffers.
crates/hardware-telemetry/src/windows_im.ownership: Device handles and COM apartments/interfaces use RAII and are released exactly once.
crates/hardware-telemetry/src/windows_im.buffer_alignment_lifetime: Mutable output buffers remain allocated for each call and parser slices are limited to bytes reported as valid.
crates/hardware-telemetry/src/windows_im.error_translation: HRESULT/Win32/unsupported-device outcomes remain explicit telemetry unavailable/error states, never synthetic health values.
crates/hardware-telemetry/src/windows_im.partial_failure_cleanup: RAII releases handles/COM state after WMI or IOCTL failure.
crates/hardware-telemetry/src/windows_im.cancellation: Provider timeouts/budgets remain authoritative and telemetry collection must not block maintenance shutdown indefinitely.

crates/idle-scheduler/src/windows_state..safety_invariant: Win32 structs are initialized with correct size/version fields, token/session handles are valid only within probe scope, and property buffers are type/length checked before conversion.
crates/idle-scheduler/src/windows_state..ownership: Any token/notification/property resource returned by Win32 is immediately scoped to its corresponding RAII/release path.
crates/idle-scheduler/src/windows_state..buffer_alignment_lifetime: Pointers reference live structs/buffers and returned byte counts gate reads.
crates/idle-scheduler/src/windows_state..error_translation: Probe uncertainty is represented as unknown/ineligible according to scheduler policy, never permissive success.
crates/idle-scheduler/src/windows_state..partial_failure_cleanup: All handles/COM allocations are released on early exits.
crates/idle-scheduler/src/windows_state..cancellation: Slow provider probes remain bounded so scheduler evaluation cannot pin worker lifetime.

crates/ipc/src/windows_impl.rs.safety_invariant: SID/security-descriptor buffers remain valid for Win32 calls, returned descriptor memory is LocalFree'd exactly once, pipe/file HANDLE ownership has one RAII owner, and thread IDs are converted to cancel handles only after worker startup handshake.
crates/ipc/src/windows_impl.rs.ownership: Raw pipe/thread/security allocation handles transfer once to File/OwnedHandle/LocalFree paths; from_raw_handle consumes ownership and must not alias another closer.
crates/ipc/src/windows_impl.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: SID and descriptor pointers are used only while their backing allocation is live; framed reads/writes are bounded by protocol limits.
crates/ipc/src/windows_impl.rs.error_translation: Access, identity, cancellation and I/O failures remain typed IPC errors; no security verification failure falls back to a weaker principal.
crates/ipc/src/windows_impl.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: Worker-start failure closes handles/joins created workers where join ownership is retained; security allocations are freed on every branch.
crates/ipc/src/windows_impl.rs.cancellation: Current synchronous CancelSynchronousIo teardown remains a native-qualification blocker until slow-peer race tests prove a bounded upper limit or transport migrates to overlapped I/O.

crates/restore-point/src/windows_impl.rs.safety_invariant: COM process security is initialized under the documented one-time policy, LoadLibrary/GetProcAddress results are checked before typed invocation, and restore status structures are correctly initialized.
crates/restore-point/src/windows_impl.rs.ownership: Loaded module ownership is scoped and released exactly once; COM initialization remains balanced by its owner.
crates/restore-point/src/windows_impl.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: Function pointer transmutation is permitted only after non-null symbol resolution to the exact declared ABI signature.
crates/restore-point/src/windows_impl.rs.error_translation: HRESULT/Win32/restore status failures are surfaced explicitly.
crates/restore-point/src/windows_impl.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: Library/COM resources release after symbol or restore-call failure.
crates/restore-point/src/windows_impl.rs.cancellation: Restore-point creation is treated as a bounded mutation phase and cancellation cannot claim rollback without Windows evidence.

crates/security/src/lib.rs.safety_invariant: Client impersonation/token queries use handles valid for the call, TOKEN_* buffers are resized from authoritative required lengths, SID comparisons only read initialized token data, and thread impersonation is always reverted.
crates/security/src/lib.rs.ownership: Token/service handles have one closer and impersonation is guarded by ThreadImpersonation/explicit revert.
crates/security/src/lib.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: TOKEN_USER/TOKEN_GROUPS typed views are created only after sufficient aligned storage has been populated.
crates/security/src/lib.rs.error_translation: Token/SID/service mismatch is authentication failure; lookup failure never grants access.
crates/security/src/lib.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: Impersonation reverts and handles close on all early-return paths.
crates/security/src/lib.rs.cancellation: Authentication is completed before session authority is retained; disconnect cannot leave impersonation active.

crates/startup-manager/src/windows_impl..safety_invariant: Registry value/name buffers honor returned lengths and types, COM task interfaces stay inside a valid apartment, service/registry handles are valid for each call, and task indices honor COM collection bounds.
crates/startup-manager/src/windows_impl..ownership: Registry/service handles and COM apartment lifetime are RAII-scoped; BSTR/VARIANT/interface ownership follows windows-rs semantics.
crates/startup-manager/src/windows_impl..buffer_alignment_lifetime: Mutable registry buffers are sized before calls; UTF-16 string pointers remain alive for synchronous APIs.
crates/startup-manager/src/windows_impl..error_translation: Registry/COM/service errors remain explicit and cannot fabricate enabled/disabled startup state.
crates/startup-manager/src/windows_impl..partial_failure_cleanup: Handles and COM state release after partial enumeration/mutation failure.
crates/startup-manager/src/windows_impl..cancellation: Provider operations must respect supervisor/read budgets and cannot bypass mutation authorization on retry.

crates/update-engine/src/platform.rs.safety_invariant: RTL_OSVERSIONINFOW and WINTRUST_DATA fields/sizes are initialized exactly for their APIs, backing path/provider structures remain live for both VERIFY and CLOSE calls, and trust state is closed on every verification attempt.
crates/update-engine/src/platform.rs.ownership: WinTrust provider state opened by VERIFY is closed exactly once with WTD_STATEACTION_CLOSE.
crates/update-engine/src/platform.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: All pointers in WINTRUST_DATA reference live stack/UTF-16 storage for the full verify/close sequence.
crates/update-engine/src/platform.rs.error_translation: Any non-success trust status is verification failure; unsigned/untrusted payloads never advance update state.
crates/update-engine/src/platform.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: WinTrust state close is attempted even after a failed verification result.
crates/update-engine/src/platform.rs.cancellation: Cancellation cannot skip Authenticode/hash/signature verification before installer handoff.

crates/windows-foundation/src/lib.rs.safety_invariant: Each wrapper accepts only handles/pointers whose ownership contract is explicit; SHGetKnownFolderPath memory is converted before CoTaskMemFree; OVERLAPPED structures remain live for synchronous LockFileEx/UnlockFileEx calls; impersonation is always reverted.
crates/windows-foundation/src/lib.rs.ownership: OwnedHandle/OwnedServiceHandle close exactly once; into_raw transfers ownership by ManuallyDrop; COM and impersonation guards balance successful acquisition.
crates/windows-foundation/src/lib.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: Wide path buffers are NUL-terminated/live for Win32 calls; CoTaskMem pointer is read before free.
crates/windows-foundation/src/lib.rs.error_translation: Win32/HRESULT results preserve lock contention vs hard error and surface failed RevertToSelf where explicit.
crates/windows-foundation/src/lib.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: RAII closes handles/uninitializes COM/reverts impersonation on early return.
crates/windows-foundation/src/lib.rs.cancellation: Background/thread state guards restore prior state on scope exit and must not outlive their originating thread.

crates/windows-pnp/src/windows_impl.rs.safety_invariant: SP_DEVINFO_DATA.cbSize is initialized, SetupAPI buffers use required-size probes and returned byte counts, property types are validated, and enumeration ends only on the documented no-more-items condition.
crates/windows-pnp/src/windows_impl.rs.ownership: HDEVINFO and related handles are destroyed exactly once through RAII.
crates/windows-pnp/src/windows_impl.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: Typed property views are created only from sufficiently sized initialized buffers; UTF-16 reads stay within returned lengths.
crates/windows-pnp/src/windows_impl.rs.error_translation: Unsupported/missing properties remain optional; API failures do not fabricate device health/state.
crates/windows-pnp/src/windows_impl.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: Device information sets close on every exit path.
crates/windows-pnp/src/windows_impl.rs.cancellation: Enumeration remains bounded by finite device sets and higher-level provider budgets.

crates/windows-update/src/execution_wind.safety_invariant: All WUA COM methods execute within a live COM apartment, collection indices remain within Count(), VARIANT/BSTR/interface lifetimes follow windows-rs ownership, and selected update identities are revalidated against fresh WUA results before install.
crates/windows-update/src/execution_wind.ownership: COM interfaces/collections are reference-counted by windows-rs and apartment lifetime encloses their use.
crates/windows-update/src/execution_wind.buffer_alignment_lifetime: No borrowed COM output is retained beyond its owning interface/value lifetime.
crates/windows-update/src/execution_wind.error_translation: HRESULT/WUA result-code failures are typed update failures; partial success cannot be promoted to full success.
crates/windows-update/src/execution_wind.partial_failure_cleanup: MutationSupervisor/update owner state and COM apartment unwind on every error path; selection is revalidated before mutation.
crates/windows-update/src/execution_wind.cancellation: Cancellation is checked at state-machine boundaries and cannot skip post-install verification/recovery accounting.

crates/windows-update/src/windows_impl.r.safety_invariant: WUA COM calls execute under a valid apartment, online search configuration/result codes are checked, collection indices stay within Count(), and metadata conversions preserve typed absence/errors.
crates/windows-update/src/windows_impl.r.ownership: windows-rs COM interfaces/BSTR/VARIANT values remain within apartment lifetime and release through reference counting.
crates/windows-update/src/windows_impl.r.buffer_alignment_lifetime: No raw COM pointer is retained outside its owning smart interface.
crates/windows-update/src/windows_impl.r.error_translation: Search/result/property HRESULT failures become explicit discovery errors; unavailable metadata is not invented.
crates/windows-update/src/windows_impl.r.partial_failure_cleanup: COM state and intermediate interfaces release on early return.
crates/windows-update/src/windows_impl.r.cancellation: Discovery remains read-budget bounded; cancellation cannot mutate driver/update state.

services/maintenance-service/src/main.rs.safety_invariant: Service control dispatcher/table callback pointers use the declared system ABI and point to static/long-lived service name/callback state for the dispatcher lifetime.
services/maintenance-service/src/main.rs.ownership: SCM callback registration does not transfer an owning kernel HANDLE to Rust at this boundary.
services/maintenance-service/src/main.rs.buffer_alignment_lifetime: UTF-16 service name and SERVICE_TABLE_ENTRYW storage remain valid while StartServiceCtrlDispatcherW consumes them.
services/maintenance-service/src/main.rs.error_translation: SCM registration/dispatcher failure aborts service startup.
services/maintenance-service/src/main.rs.partial_failure_cleanup: Service runtime state is not published before dispatcher registration succeeds.
services/maintenance-service/src/main.rs.cancellation: Stop/control callbacks feed the bounded shutdown path; callback registration itself does not weaken shutdown authority.
